name: observational-memory
description: Compaction as observational memory: in the background, after each turn and during a long one, an Observer (GPT-5.6 Luna through pi) turns each ~10k-token chunk of the conversation (up to four at once) into attributed, prioritized observations, each with the transcript time range it came from, keeping tool errors and the head and tail of long results; a reply that is incomplete or malformed is never stored, and a Reflector condenses the observations when they grow, to a size it is checked against. Compaction cuts at the observed watermark with no model call; where the Observer has not observed enough, has failed or its memory is over budget, a session brief compiled by code from the unobserved rows (goal, files, commits, outstanding items and a log, each line naming the om_recall block it came from) stands in place of the built-in compaction and fits one total budget for the model's window: it keeps recent messages whole, the user's messages verbatim, the user's constraints in force (a reversal replaces what it names, a repeat is one line, and constraints over their cap fall back to the built-in compaction rather than drop any), one continuation record of what is active, completed, blocked or waiting for the user, and the instructions given to /compact; a decision waiting for the user stays a question. Skills in use are carried across compactions, and an om_recall tool, kept out of the deferred tool list once a compaction has run and named at the end of the memory as the way to recover any detail the observations lack, searches (ranking lines that hold a searched term whole first), reads and outlines the full transcript, lists the files the session read, edited or wrote, following a session across moved transcript files, skipping replayed and injected text, and saying what it covered and did not; om_stats and /om-stats report usage per session, and sessions untouched for 30 days are pruned from the store, checked again just before each deletion.
